instruction.text: Draw a line from Norway to Orkney.

end.text: After their first raid on Lindisfarne, the Vikings continued to attack Britain. As it only took one or two days to sail there, they soon came across Orkney, a group of islands at the very top of Scotland.
end.sound: ssml: After their first raid on Lindisfarne, the Vikings continued to attack Britain. As it only took one or two days to sail there, they soon came across Orknee, a group of islands at the very top of Scotland.

atoms.b: As Orkney was so close to ((++Norway France)), and there was free land, the Vikings chose to settle there with their families.

The islands were surrounded by sea, which made it ((++hard fun)) for other people to attack. The land was also fertile, and there were lots of fish in the sea, so the Vikings could ((++farm fry)) and eat.
Orkney was the ((++ideal worst)) place for the Vikings to settle. For many years, they used Orkney as a base for their ((++raids peace)) on Scotland, Ireland and England.

instruction.text: Where is the Isle of Sheppey?

feedback.end: In AD 835, the Vikings raided the rich monasteries on the Isle of Sheppey. This was the first major raid in the South of England.

instruction.text: Despite the raids, not everybody in Britain was afraid of the Vikings. Listen and select the correct sentence endings.

atoms.a: For a long time, Cornwall had been in conflict ...

b.sound: with the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Wessex.

atoms.a: After seeing the Vikings raid and threaten Wessex, ...

b.sound: Cornwall decided to team up with the Vikings.

atoms.a: Why do you think the Vikings might have helped the Cornish?

atoms.b: Tin is an important metal that has been mined in ((++Cornwall deserts)) for over 4,000 years. In exchange for the Vikings’ help, it is likely that the Cornish people ((++traded stole)) tin.

feedback.end: This alliance was ultimately unsuccessful. In AD 838, at the Battle of Hingston Down, the Cornish and Vikings lost to Wessex.

atoms.a: The Cornish and Vikings fought the Anglo-Saxons of Wessex.
